I farm 20 mu, and at my age I will not make the whole place too complicated. I will keep the main body in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest cash and grain flow here, and I will leave a smaller block for cotton because I know how to manage it and I have well water. Since some people in the house work off-farm, I have to think about labor as well as yield, so I will use hybrid maize, a good improved wheat variety, and an improved cotton variety that has stable boll setting. I start from what has worked in recent years, then I adjust by cost and by field condition. I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because losing yield costs me more than wasting a little bag of fertilizer. On the wheat-maize land, I will keep phosphorus and potassium in the base dressing and then push nitrogen according to yield target. Wheat needs a firmer start and one topdressing at jointing. Maize needs enough nitrogen early and around the big trumpet stage. Cotton I will not overdo nitrogen too late, or it runs to stalk and leaf, so I will hold potassium a bit higher for boll setting. I have well irrigation, so I will use water at the key stages instead of gambling on rain. For tillage, I will keep wheat land under rotary tillage, push maize with no-tillage after wheat to save labor and catch moisture, and I will plough the cotton block once because cotton likes a cleaner, deeper seedbed. My target is steady output, not chasing the very top yield with very high cost.
